title: Machine learning on voice and facial features identifies early-stage Parkinson's disease
summary: Smartphone recordings of voice and facial expressions from 371 participants were analysed with nine machine-learning classifiers. Integrated features discriminated early-stage Parkinson's disease patients from controls with an AUROC of 0.85, and 0.90 in a validation cohort of 74 patients and 74 controls.
ai_technology: Nine machine-learning classifiers on integrated voice and facial-expression features

evidence.tested: Training cohort (112 PD, 111 controls) and validation cohort (74 PD, 74 controls).
evidence.unknown: Validation cohort is from the same study and recorded in a different medication phase; abstract only; full text not reviewed.
evidence.ai_role: Machine-learning classifiers combined acoustic and facial features to separate patients from controls.
